subject: Materials Science
title: Earthenware, Stoneware, and Porcelain
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Earthenware, Stoneware, and Porcelain.

hook.text: A terra-cotta pot chips easily. A porcelain teacup rings like a bell. Firing temperature is the difference.

buildup.text: Earthenware fires at 1,000°C — porous and soft, like flower pots and bricks.

discovery.text: Stoneware fires at 1,200°C — denser and waterproof, used for crocks and dinnerware.

twist.text: Porcelain fires at 1,400°C with kaolin clay — so dense it becomes translucent.

climax.text: China guarded porcelain secrets for centuries — Europe only cracked the recipe in 1708.

punchline.text: Hotter fire, finer clay — from flowerpot to fine china.

quiz.question: What makes porcelain different from earthenware?
options: Porcelain uses metal powder instead of clay
Porcelain is fired at higher temperatures with kaolin clay
Earthenware is fired at higher temperatures
